punchline: In the scanner, the brain's alarm lit up while the area that turns experience into words went quiet.
thirty_sec: Bessel van der Kolk scanned people with trauma histories while they listened to a description of their own experience. The amygdala, the alarm centre, surged. Broca's area, which helps produce speech, went quiet. His reading is that the body reacts first and words can fail, which is why he thinks talking alone may not be enough.
